name: VariableProximity-TS-TW
title: Variable Proximity
description: Two lines of a sentence sit on black, and each letter grows heavier and wider the closer the pointer comes, easing back to thin as it moves away.
use: A display headline should feel alive and reward the pointer without moving from its place.
avoid: Paragraph text or touch-only screens: it needs a pointer and a variable font.
a11y: A hidden copy of the sentence serves screen readers, but there is no reduced-motion handling. (keyboard: n-a, labels: good, reduced motion: not handled)
looks: Two centred lines of white type, one large and one smaller, sit on a black stage. Within each line some letters are broad and bold while their neighbours stay light and narrow.
behaves: Wherever the pointer goes, letters within a certain radius thicken and stretch, strongest right under the cursor and fading outward. Moving away lets them return to a thin width.
customise: The label, from and to font settings, radius, falloff curve, class names and a click handler are props. The page must load the variable font.
weight: moderate: An animation-frame loop restyles every letter as the pointer moves.
